name: Linear
tagline: Create a public Linear OAuth app and plug it into Composio. No review, live in minutes.

cost.asStated: Free. Linear: "It does not cost anything to develop agents in Linear."

steps.title: Set up your Composio account
steps.when: Skip if you already have a Composio project and API key.
instructions: Sign up from the Composio login page.
Open Settings → API keys and copy a key.
Save it as COMPOSIO_API_KEY where your agent runs.
Stay in this project. Auth configs belong to one project.

problems.q: I can't find the API keys page
a: Open the API keys link above after signing in. It opens Settings → API keys for your current project.
If you have several projects, switch to the one you'll use for this agent first.

steps.title: Choose the workspace that owns the app
instructions: Linear recommends a separate workspace just for the app. Every admin there can manage it.
You must be a workspace admin. On the Free plan every member is an admin.
Not an admin? Find one with Cmd/Ctrl K → View workspace admins, or create a new workspace.

steps.title: Create a public OAuth app
instructions: Open the pre-filled link below. Or: Settings → Administration → API → create a new OAuth application.
Fill in the values below. Your app name and icon are what users see on the consent screen.
Turn Public on. Apps are private by default and only install in your own workspace.
Leave client credentials off. Composio uses the normal user sign-in flow.
Save the app.

fields.label: Application name
fields.hint: 2–80 characters. Can't contain "Linear" or a URL

fields.label: Callback URL
fields.hint: Must match your Composio auth config exactly

fields.label: Public
fields.hint: Lets other workspaces install the app

warnings.text: Linear's agent docs say to submit to the directory to reach other workspaces. For a user-actor app, Public is enough.
warnings.unconfirmed: We didn't install a public app from a second workspace to prove no directory listing is needed.

steps.unconfirmed: Field labels come from Linear's manifest docs. We couldn't open the form or check the pre-fill without signing in.

problems.q: I can't see the API page in Settings
a: Settings → Administration → API needs workspace admin permissions.
Ask an admin to make you one, or create the app in a workspace you own.

problems.q: Users in other workspaces can't install the app
a: The app is still private, Linear's default.
Open the app's settings and turn Public on.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and secret
instructions: On the app's page, copy the Client ID and Client secret.
Store the secret in a secret manager, never in git.
Leaked? Use Rotate secret next to the client secret. Existing user tokens keep working.

a: Linear didn't accept the Client ID and secret Composio sent.
Copy both again from the app page, or rotate the secret, then update your Composio auth config.

steps.title: Choose scopes
instructions: Linear scopes aren't set on the app. You list them in the Composio auth config next.
read is always included. Add write to update issues, projects and more.
Only create things? Use issues:create and comments:create instead of write.
Skip admin unless a tool truly needs it. Linear says never to ask for it otherwise.
steps.agentTask: Find the Linear tools my code calls and suggest the narrowest scopes to paste into the auth config.

warnings.text: Composio's Linear setup adds admin by default. Remove it unless you need admin endpoints.
Linear also offers actor=app, which acts as the app instead of the user. It needs an admin to install and bars the admin scope.
warnings.unconfirmed: We couldn't confirm a Composio setting for actor=app. Connections act as the signed-in user by default.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config
instructions: Open the Linear toolkit in Composio and create an auth config.
Use the values below, then paste your Client ID and Client secret.
Set the Redirect URI explicitly. Some toolkit defaults still use an older callback.
Replace the default scopes with your list. Remove admin unless you need it.
Save, then copy the auth config ID (ac_…) for the next step.

fields.label: Redirect URI
fields.hint: Must match the Callback URL in Linear exactly

fields.label: Scopes
fields.hint: Same list as the previous step

warnings.text: Composio's Linear guide still shows the old callback /api/v1/auth-apps/add. Use the v3 URL in both places.

steps.unconfirmed: The link exists. We couldn't check, without logging in, whether it opens auth config creation directly. If not: Auth Configs → Create Auth Config.

problems.q: Connecting fails with a redirect URI mismatch
a: The auth config's Redirect URI doesn't match the Callback URL on your Linear app.
Set both to the v3 Composio callback exactly. The old v1 default won't match.

problems.q: The link didn't open the Linear toolkit
a: Open Auth Configs in the Composio dashboard and click Create Auth Config.
Pick Linear, choose OAuth2, and turn on your own developer credentials.

steps.title: Use the auth config in your agent
instructions: Pass the auth config ID when you create a session. Your coding agent can paste this in.
Toolkits you don't list keep using Composio's managed auth.

a: The session must include authConfigs with your ac_… ID for linear.
Toolkits not listed in authConfigs fall back to managed auth.

steps.title: Connect a test account
instructions: Start a connection for a test user and open the link.
The consent screen should show your app name, not Composio.
Try a user from a second workspace too. That proves Public is on.
Users already connected through managed auth must reconnect.

warnings.text: Since April 1, 2026 every Linear app gets 24-hour access tokens plus a refresh token. Each refresh returns a new refresh token.
warnings.unconfirmed: Composio says it refreshes OAuth tokens. We didn't test a Linear refresh end to end.

steps.unconfirmed: We didn't run a full connection. It needs a Composio API key and a real Linear sign-in.

problems.q: The consent screen still says Composio
a: The connection used the managed auth config. Pass your ac_… ID in the session.
Existing connections keep their old config. Delete and reconnect them.

problems.q: A tool fails with a permissions error
a: The token lacks a scope that tool needs, e.g. write to update issues.
Add the scope in your Composio auth config, then have the user reconnect.

problems.q: A connection stopped working after the user revoked it
a: Users can remove apps under Settings → Account → Security & Access → Authorized applications.
Have them connect again.

steps.title: Get approved in your user's workspace
steps.when: Only if a user's paid Linear workspace requires approval for third-party apps.
instructions: The user tries to connect. Linear shows a screen to request approval, with an optional reason.
Their workspace admin (owner on Enterprise) gets an email and in-app notification.
The admin approves it from the link, or in Settings → Applications.
The user gets notified, then connects again.
steps.unconfirmed: We had no paid workspace with approvals on, so we didn't see the request screen during a Composio connection.

problems.q: The user was told the app was denied
a: An admin denied it earlier. Linear shows the reason they gave.
Address the reason with their admin, who can approve it in Settings → Applications.

steps.title: List in the Integration Directory
steps.when: Only if you want Linear users to find you in the directory. Not needed for OAuth to work.
instructions: Fill out Linear's submission form. It includes a sample page for copy style and length.
Send assets to integrations@linear.app or link them in the form.
Color and white icons 320×320, plus 1–3 showcase images 1600×1000.
Linear accepts integrations from formal companies. Hobby or low-effort apps are usually declined.
Linear states no review timeline.
